summary: Tested the new per-user ad-paywall feature (unlocked_ids) gating 3 lazily-AI-generated content types: career description, roadmap-task resources, daily-plan-item resources. Backend: 2 new pytest tests for GET /api/content/unlock-status and POST /api/content/unlock pass (free user gated per-id, premium always unlocked). Frontend: all 3 gates verified end-to-end for free user (test_ui_fresh@test.pl) - teaser shown on first open, ad-then-reveal flow works, persists unlocked on re-open of same content, re-gates a different content id - and for premium user (ania_t1@test.pl) - zero gates/ads anywhere, content shown immediately. No regressions found; backend/expo logs clean (all 200s), no red screens.
action_items: No blocking issues found. Feature works exactly as specified by the user's requirement.
critical_code_review_comments: useContentUnlock.ts hook correctly optimistically sets react-query cache to {unlocked:true} immediately after watchAd() succeeds (before the POST /content/unlock call resolves), so UI reveal feels instant; POST failure is swallowed (non-fatal comment explains rationale) - acceptable tradeoff, worst case user re-watches an ad once.

GET /content/unlock-status query is `enabled: !!contentId && !isPremium` - correctly skips the network call entirely for premium users (isPremium short-circuits unlocked=true in the hook), avoiding unnecessary backend calls - good perf choice.

Verified via direct backend calls + packet inspection in supervisor logs: GET /api/content/unlock-status?id=task:45d1f522f1 returned 200 before POST /api/content/unlock, and task resources endpoint was only called after the unlock POST succeeded - sequencing matches intended UX (ad before content fetch to avoid wasting the AI call on users who abandon the ad).

career/[id].tsx, TaskSheet.tsx, plan.tsx DailyItemSheet all follow the identical pattern (useContentUnlock + AdUnlockGate + `enabled: unlocked` on the underlying content query) - good consistency/DRY across the 3 integration points.

Content IDs are correctly namespaced per content-type (`career:<id>`, `task:<id>`, `daily:<id>`) preventing collisions across the three different unlock gates sharing one unlocked_ids array on the user doc.
seed_data_creation: test_ui_fresh@test.pl: completed the 10-question quiz and generated recommendations (via the quiz ad-gate from a prior session's work, unrelated to this feature) to get a usable career list for testing; unlocked 1 career ('Specjalista ds. obsługi klienta B2B') and 1 roadmap task ('Kurs podstaw grafiki komputerowej') via the new ad-gate as part of testing. ania_t1@test.pl: generated a new daily study plan via 'Ułóż mój plan dzienny' (premium, no ad) to test the daily-item-unlock-gate path, which was previously untested for this account.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature fully verified both backend and frontend. Free user test_ui_fresh@test.pl now has: 1 career unlocked (career:<id of Specjalista ds. obsługi klienta B2B>), 1 task unlocked, and an active roadmap for a custom career 'test_grafik komputerowy'. Premium ania_t1@test.pl now additionally has a daily study plan (was missing before). No regressions observed in login, quiz, recommendations generation, roadmap building, or daily/weekly plan flows - all returned 200s in backend logs during this session with zero errors in expo logs.
rca_of_issue: N/A - no bugs found. Feature behaves exactly per the user's explicit requirement: per-user first-view ad-gate independent of whether another user already triggered the underlying AI generation and cached it in career_templates; premium always bypasses; unlock persists server-side per user across different content types (career/task/daily) using namespaced IDs in a single unlocked_ids array.
